svg.text: Modules as photographed 2026-11-04. I2C section matches the bench build of 2026-11-03 (scan: 0x1C 0x3C 0x57 0x6A). Buttons, LED and buzzer are the planned connections, not yet tested.
Pin names are the Arduino names printed on the Nano ESP32 header. All logic is 3.3 V. A dot is a junction; a crossing without a dot is not a connection.
on-board 3.3 V LDO feeds the 3V3 pin
5 V over its built-in USB-C cable
reserved: GY-MAX30102 INT (not wired in v1, polling used)
reserved: 4517 INT1 data-ready (not wired in v1)
10 k pull-ups to 3.3 V on board
I2C 0x57; INT pin left open (see D8)
4.7 k pull-ups to on-board 1.8 V: measure bus high level
pin order GND VCC SCL SDA (silkscreen, photo 2026-11-04)
J1 Grove 4-pin; Q1 transistor drives BUZ1
or a cut Grove cable. HIGH on SIG = sound.
Alternative: use the on-board RGB LED (LED_RED etc., active low) and drop this net.
1. Power: Nano only from USB-C. No VIN, no bare LiPo. 3V3 pin supplies every module.
2. One I2C bus at 400 kHz: 0x6A, 0x1C, 0x57, 0x3C. Confirmed by 03_i2c_scan on 2026-11-03.
3. Bus high level: 4517 10 k to 3.3 V in parallel with MAX30102 4.7 k to 1.8 V gives about 2.7 V.
Measure SDA/SCL high with a meter; below 2.5 V, move or remove the MAX30102 pull-ups.
4. Buttons: three kit pushbuttons, one leg to the pin, the other to GND. Debounce in firmware.
5. Buzzer and LED pins are the ones used by firmware/bringup/07_oled_buttons.
6. Not drawn: Grove vibration motor (D6, only if available), UNO R4 bench board,
ADXL335 backup, LIS3MDL magnetometer (same board, not used).
Source: hardware/wiring/README.md net list. Regenerate from gen_schematic.py if pins change.
